title: Your prompt is the problem: before and after

sources.name: Prompting guidance: be specific about task, context and format

caption:
Most weak AI answers start with a weak prompt. Here are two before-and-after examples you can copy.
Be specific about the task, the audience and the format, then check the result yourself.
Save this checklist. Comment BETTER and I will send the before-and-after list.

slides.headline: Vague in, vague out
body: The more specific the request, the more useful the draft.

slides.headline: Too vague
body: Nothing here says who it is for or what you need.
slides.prompt: Write an email about the meeting.

slides.headline: Specific and usable
body: Now it knows the audience, tone and next step.
slides.prompt: Write a short email to my team moving Friday's meeting to Monday at 10am. Friendly tone. Ask them to reply if Monday does not work.

slides.headline: Constraints help
body: Limits make the answer fit your real life.
slides.prompt: Give me 5 dinner ideas for two people, under 30 minutes, with no oven. We like chicken and rice. Include one vegetarian option.

slides.headline: Say what shape the answer takes
body: Table, bullets, steps or short paragraphs. Pick one.
slides.prompt: Put the answer in a table with columns for the idea, the time needed and the main ingredients.

slides.headline: Say what to leave out
body: Length limits and exclusions stop rambling answers.
slides.prompt: Keep it under 150 words. Skip the introduction and do not suggest anything that needs special equipment.

slides.headline: Before you hit send
body: Did you say who it is for?
Did you ask for a format?

slides.headline: Save this prompt checklist
body: Comment BETTER and I will send the before-and-after list.
Share this with someone who types one-line prompts.
